chapter_theme: Understanding as protection and as practice: it steers the mind, tests what is heard, moves with the world, foresees what is coming and knows what to fear. After three chapters on acquiring knowledge, this one asks what it is to have it.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar's divisions: the distinction of understanding (421), its definition (422-426), those who have it (427-428), and what they are spared and possess (429-430).

421.reading: Understanding is the tool that guards against அற்றம், and an inner fortress enemies can't destroy.
421.nuance: The fort is one of the six limbs of a kingdom (381). This verse puts a fort inside the person, with உள் able to mean either inward or impenetrable from within, as Parimelazhagar notes.

positions.position: அற்றம் is final ruin, which understanding foresees and prevents.
positions.quote: அரசர்க்கு அறிவு என்பது இறுதி வாராமல் காக்கும் கருவியாம்

positions.position: அற்றம் is one's own weakness, and understanding covers one's faults, while the fort handles harm from others.
positions.quote: இது தனக்குள்ள குற்றத்தை மறைக்கு மென்றும், பிறரால் வரும் தீமை யைக் காக்குமென்றும்

422.reading: Understanding does not let one go wherever things have gone, but turns away from evil and steers toward good.
422.nuance: The verse doesn't name what wanders. Both commentators supply the mind, but they disagree on what is held back and how far.

positions.position: The mind itself is driven through the senses, as a groom drives a horse. Understanding is a separate quality of the soul.
positions.quote: குதிரையை நிலமறிந்து செலுத்தும் வாதுவன்போல வேறாக்கி மனத்தைப் புலமறிந்து செலுத்துவது அறிவு

positions.position: The mind may go, but the body must not follow it, and the verse chiefly concerns sexual pleasure.

423.reading: Whatever is heard, from whoever's mouth, understanding is seeing the true substance of that very thing.
423.nuance: The repeated யார்யார் removes the speaker from the test. Parimelazhagar gives the sharp consequence: high matters may come from low mouths, harmful ones from friends. He takes மெய்ப்பொருள் as the thing's true use, not its truth in the abstract, which Manakkudavar and Kalaignar prefer.

424.reading: Understanding is saying things so they go in easily, while seeing the subtle meaning in what comes from others.
424.nuance: The two directions are asymmetric: speech should make the hard simple, and listening should find the fine in the plain. Parimelazhagar goes further, saying to take the use from what others say even if it is flawed in expression.

425.reading: Embracing the world is brightness; not opening and closing is understanding.
425.nuance: Parimelazhagar narrows உலகம் to the worthy and contrasts a pond flower that closes with a tree flower that stays open.

positions.position: What must not open and close is friendship with the worthy. He records another view that it is about wealth and poverty.
positions.quote: அந்நட்பின்கண் முன் மலர்தலும் பின் கூம்புதலும் இன்றி ஒரு நிலையினாவது அறிவாம்.

positions.position: What must not open and close is one's response to joy and sorrow, which is equanimity.
positions.quote: இன்பம் துன்பம் ஆகிய இரண்டையும் ஒரே நிலையாகக் கருதுவதே

426.reading: As the world lives, so to live with the world is understanding.
426.nuance: This verse needs reading with 423, because the same chapter tells the reader to test everything and to go along.

positions.position: It restrains a king: he must not think that because he commands the world, no one commands him.
உலகம் means the elevated of earlier times, so this is following the worthy, not the crowd.
positions.quote: முற்பட்ட உயர்ந்தாரோடு பொருந்த ஒழுகுதல் அறிவு என்றார்.

427.reading: Those with understanding know what will come to be; those without it cannot.
427.nuance: ஆவது could be what will happen or what is good for oneself; Parimelazhagar records both. His gloss makes foreknowledge an act of reasoning ahead, எண்ணி அறிதல், and not prophecy. Not knowing is defined as finding out once it arrives.

428.reading: Not fearing what is to be feared is folly; fearing what is to be feared is the work of the knowing.
428.nuance: Fear is treated as a skill, தொழில். Parimelazhagar and Manakkudavar both notice the conflict with the kingly fearlessness of 382 and resolve it. Parimelazhagar defines fear here as considering and refraining.

429.reading: Those whose understanding guards against what is coming have no affliction that comes to shake them.
429.nuance: அதிர வருவது is careful: the claim may be that no calamity shakes them, not that no calamity comes. Parimelazhagar's guarding means removing the cause.

positions.position: Even suffering from past deeds does not come harshly if it is guarded against early.
positions.quote: இது முன்னை வினையால் வருந் துன்பமும் முற்பட்டுக் காக்கின், கடிதாக வாராதென்றது.

430.reading: Those with understanding have everything; those without it have nothing, whatever they have.
430.nuance: Parimelazhagar gives a practical reason, not a pious one: all wealth is made and kept by understanding, so the fool has no means of keeping what he has or rebuilding it.

links.note: Nearly the same second line. 355 tests a thing regardless of how it appears; 423 tests it regardless of who says it. Together they strip away both of the surfaces that mislead: appearance and authority.

423 sets aside the speaker when judging what is said. 415 rests the value of words on the speaker's conduct, and Parimelazhagar says those lacking it shouldn't be heard. Who says it either doesn't matter or matters most.

In the same chapter, 423 demands testing every claim for yourself and 426 says live as the world lives. The tension is softened if உலகம் means the worthy, as Manakkudavar has it, but the verse doesn't say so.

380 says fate arrives first even when one devises another way; 429 says foresight spares one from being shaken. Manakkudavar faces this directly, allowing that early guarding softens even what comes from past deeds.

374 separates being wealthy from being wise. In Parimelazhagar's gloss on 430, all wealth is made and kept by understanding, while his gloss on 374 draws the conclusion that wealth doesn't need wisdom as its cause.
Both turn on அற்றம். Understanding is the inner fort against it, and one's own fault is the enemy that brings it. So the attacker and the defence are both within.
